blockHints.patient_biodata: Only basic patient identifiers example: 'John Doe, 35'
blockHints.opening_sentence: The presenting complaint the patient opens the station with example: 'I've been having a lot of pain in my right leg for the past few weeks and it's been getting worse'
blockHints.expanded_history: Detailed information about the concern example: 'The pain is worse when I walk or stand for long periods and it's been getting worse over the past few weeks. I've also noticed that my leg is swollen and it's been getting more painful over the past few days. I've been taking ibuprofen to help with the pain, but it's not been helping much. The swelling gets a bit better when I lie down, but it comes back when I get up again. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping at night because of the pain and its beginnig to affect my work and social life.'
blockHints.family_social_history: Detailed information about any relevant family history example: 'My mother has high blood pressure and my father has diabetes', 'i live with my wife and two children', 'I'm a smoker', 'I'm a heavy drinker/occasionally take alcohol', 'works as a bus driver'
blockHints.past_med_history_allergies: Detailed information about any relevant past medical history example: 'I had a broken leg when I was 10 years old and I've had a few surgeries on my knee',  'I'm allergic to penicillin', 'I have no allergies', 'No relevant past medical history', 'i on amlodipine for hypertension'
blockHints.idea: Patient's thoughts about the presenting complaint example: 'I'm worried that the pain may be due to the multiple surgeries I've had on my knee'
blockHints.concerns: Patient's worries about the presenting complaint example: 'I'm worried that the pain may be due to the multiple surgeries I've had on my knee', 'could this be a sign of something more serious?'
blockHints.expectation: Patient's expectations from the consultation example: 'I'm hoping the doctor can help me figure out what's causing the pain and give me some advice on how to manage it'
blockHints.persona: The personality to adopt during the consultation example: A bit nervous about the consultation, but open to discussing concerns
blockHints.questions: Questions the patient asks the doctor example: 'What could be causing the pain? Is there anything I can do to make it better?,  'can this be cancer?', 'should i be worried about this?'
blockHints.recent_notes: Only critical/emergency-relevant previous notes, if any. Usually empty. example: 'Recent ER visit for chest pain', 'Recent visit for knee pain, planned for an MRI'
blockHints.current_medications: Only essential current medications, if any. Usually empty. example: 'Warfarin', '', 'Amlodipine 10mg OD', 'Apixaban 5mg OD'
blockHints.past_medical_history: Only relevant past medical history, if any. Usually empty. example: 'had a broken leg at 10 years old', 'had a stroke 5 years ago'
blockHints.recent_investigations: Only recent investigations, if any. Usually empty. example: 'recent x-ray showed a fracture', 'recent blood test showed high cholesterol'
blockHints.social_history: Only relevant social history, if any. Usually empty. example: 'lives alone'
blockHints.explanation: Explanation of the diagnosis or condition to the patient using MUACLW ATRAIN format example: 'I understand you're concerned about the pain in your leg and how it's affecting your daily activities. From examining your leg, I can see that you have a muscle strain, which means some of the muscle fibers have been stretched or slightly torn. Think of it like a rubber band that's been stretched too far - it becomes sore and needs time to recover. This is actually a common injury that we see quite often. The good news is that muscle strains typically heal well with the right care and management. There are several effective ways to help with the pain and support your recovery, including rest, gentle exercises, and pain relief. I'd  go through these treatment options with you and also refer you to a physiotherapist who can help guide your recovery.'
blockHints.assessment:
Focused history taking. Example for suspected DVT:
        1) Confirming Diagnosis:
        - Character of leg pain/swelling
        - Onset and progression
        - Unilateral vs bilateral
        - Risk factors (travel/surgery/immobility/OCPs)

        2) Ruling out red Flags:
        - Chest pain/breathlessness (PE)
        - Fever/rigors (infection)
        - Severe pain/numbness (compartment syndrome)
        - Recent trauma/surgery

        3) Questions for Differentials: 
        - Ask about SOB/chest pain/palpitations (PE)
        - Assess if any redness/warmth/fever (cellulitis)
        - Ask about recent injury/trauma (muscle tear/fracture)
        - Ask about morning stiffness/joint pain (arthritis)
        - Ask about history of varicose veins/chronic swelling (venous insufficiency)
        - Ask about calf pain worse on walking/better with rest (claudication)
        - Night cramps/rest pain (peripheral vascular disease)
        - Recent medication changes (drug-induced edema)
blockHints.social_concerns: Address any social concerns or challenges identified during the consultation with specific, practical steps. Example: 'I can provide you with a fit note for 2 weeks to help manage your work situation. We can also refer you to our social prescriber who can help with: 1) Applying for PIP benefits if eligible 2) Connecting you with local support groups 3) Arranging transportation assistance through community services. Additionally, I can write a letter to your housing officer explaining your medical needs for ground floor accommodation.'
blockHints.ice: Address the Patient's Ideas, Concerns, and Expectations with specific actions. Example: 'I understand your worry about cancer given your family history. Let me explain why I think this is unlikely: [specific reasons]. To give you peace of mind, I'll arrange these specific tests: [list tests]. While we wait for results, here's what we can do to help your symptoms: 1) Start with [specific treatment] 2) Monitor your symptoms using this diary sheet 3) Book a follow-up in 2 weeks to review progress.'
blockHints.immediate_actions:
Immediate clinical actions. Example for suspected DVT:
        1) Focused Examination:
        - Vital signs (BP/HR/RR/O2/Temp)
        - Affected leg:
            * Swelling/warmth/tenderness
            * Calf circumference comparison
            * Peripheral pulses/capillary refill
        - Basic cardiorespiratory exam if PE suspected
        - Wells score calculation

        2) Urgent Tests:
        - D-dimer if Wells score indicates
        - Doppler ultrasound
        - Basic bloods (FBC/Coag/U&E)
        - ECG/CXR if PE suspected

        3) Urgent Referrals:
        - Vascular team if high-risk
        - Same-day ultrasound
        - Emergency admission if PE suspected
blockHints.pharmacological_treatment: Details of medications prescribed with specific doses, durations, and monitoring plans. Example: '1) Start Levothyroxine 25mcg OD for 2 weeks, then increase to 50mcg OD - Take on empty stomach 30 mins before breakfast - Explain gradual dose titration plan - Provide written information about medication 2) Continue current medications: - Amlodipine 5mg OD - Arrange medication review in 6 weeks 3) Discuss potential side effects: - Signs of over-replacement - When to seek advice'
blockHints.non_pharmacological_treatment: Specific non-drug interventions with clear action plans. Example: '1) Refer to NHS weight management service: - Complete referral form today - Provide contact details and expected waiting time - Give interim dietary advice leaflet 2) Refer to practice-based social prescriber for: - Exercise on prescription scheme - Local support groups - Benefits advice 3) Provide specific lifestyle advice: - Structured exercise plan starting with 10-minute daily walks - Sleep hygiene measures - Stress management techniques'
blockHints.follow_up: Follow-up plan within primary care setting example: 'Book routine follow-up appointment in 2 weeks', 'Telephone review with GP in 1 week', 'Review with practice nurse for BP check in 4 weeks', 'Return to surgery if no improvement in 3 days', 'Arrange blood tests before next review'
blockHints.health_education: Detailed patient education points with specific resources. Example: '1) Provide written information: - NHS thyroid condition leaflet - Thyroid UK support group details - Dietary advice sheet 2) Demonstrate: - How to check pulse rate - Using symptom diary 3) Review lifestyle factors: - Importance of regular medication - Diet modifications needed - Exercise recommendations with specific examples 4) Direct to specific online resources: - NHS thyroid page (provide URL) - Patient.info thyroid section'
blockHints.safety_netting: Comprehensive safety-netting advice with specific symptoms and actions. Example: 'Seek urgent medical attention if: 1) Severe chest pain or breathing difficulties - Call 999 immediately - Take GTN if prescribed 2) Contact GP surgery within 24-48 hours if: - Increasing ankle swelling - New palpitations - Severe headaches 3) Book routine appointment if: - No improvement in symptoms after 6 weeks - Side effects from medication - Questions about treatment plan 4) Out of hours: - Call 111 if concerned - Local walk-in center details provided'
blockHints.additional_notes: Additional notes example: 'Patient very engaged in management plan', 'May need longer term follow-up due to complex social situation', 'Consider referral to specialist if no improvement after initial treatment course'
blockHints.doctor_patient_biodata: Only basic patient identifiers example: 'John Doe, 35'
